overview: The Hyena-class Bomber is a droid bomber whose service history spans Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). A Separatist strike bomber derived from vulture droid architecture, used to saturate Republic capital ships. Imperial archives, Rebel intelligence briefings, and Mandalorian shipyard records estimate total production at ~45,000 units, though wartime losses and black-market refits make exact counts difficult to verify.
history:
Design bureaus first drafted the Hyena-class Bomber during the political tensions that defined Clone Wars (22–19 BBY). Engineers prioritised capabilities suited to its role as a droid bomber, balancing armour, manoeuvrability, and crew requirements against the industrial capacity of the factions that ordered it into production.

As fleet doctrine evolved, the Hyena-class Bomber entered front-line service in convoy escort, planetary assault, and deep-space patrol missions. A Separatist strike bomber derived from vulture droid architecture, used to saturate Republic capital ships. Veterans praised its reliability under fire while analysts debated whether mass production at ~45,000 units diluted quality control across shipyard lines.

Major campaigns cemented the vessel's reputation — whether as a terror weapon, a rebel lifeline, or a smuggler's last hope. Battle damage reports show the droid bomber could absorb punishment that would destroy lighter craft, though attrition rates climbed sharply during the bloodiest years of galactic war.

In the modern era, surviving hulls appear in private collections, museum orbits, and covert fleets. Restorers hunt spare parts across scrap worlds while historians argue the Hyena-class Bomber symbolises the industrial scale of conflict more than any single battle honour.
significance:
The Hyena-class Bomber illustrates how shipwright traditions and wartime desperation combine to shape galactic warfare. Its droid bomber layout influenced successor designs long after production lines fell silent.

Approximately ~45,000 units hulls served during Clone Wars (22–19 BBY), making the class one of the most visible symbols of its faction's naval power. Colour markings and unit insignia turned anonymous factory output into icons recognised across holonet broadcasts.

For engineers and tacticians, the Hyena-class Bomber remains a case study in trade-offs between firepower, crew survival, and maintenance — lessons still taught at academies from Coruscant to Mandalore.
